key_facts.answer: Moving a pet from Dubai to Canada means meeting the CFIA import requirements — for dogs the central document is a valid rabies vaccination certificate matched to the pet's microchip, plus the standard UAE export documents. There is no quarantine; the real risk is an inexact certificate flagged at the CFIA inspection on arrival.

takeaways: Meet the CFIA import requirements; for dogs the key document is a valid rabies vaccination certificate.
No quarantine — the risk is an inexact certificate, not a holding period.
An ISO microchip ties the records together; record it before the vaccination certificate.
Requirements differ for cats vs dogs and personal vs commercial import — confirm your category.
Typical cost Dubai → Canada: roughly AED 14,000–20,000, about 4–6 weeks.

sections.heading: The short answer
paragraphs: To bring a pet into Canada from Dubai you need to meet the CFIA import requirements — for dogs, the central one is a valid rabies vaccination certificate with the right detail, plus the standard UAE export documents. There is no quarantine.

Canada's process is lighter than Australia's, but it's exacting: a rabies certificate missing a detail (dates, microchip number, vet signature) can hold your pet at inspection. Confirm the current CFIA requirements for your pet type before you travel.

sections.heading: What CFIA requires
paragraphs: The Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) sets the import requirements, and an inspection happens on arrival. For dogs from the UAE, the central requirement is a valid rabies vaccination certificate that matches your pet's microchip and shows the right dates and vet details.

Because requirements vary by pet type and by whether the move is personal or commercial, confirm your exact category with CFIA before booking — that one check prevents almost every Canada-route problem.

sections.heading: Your documents, in order
paragraphs: Sequenced chronologically, the requirements already named for this route fall into a clear order:
1. ISO microchip — implanted first, because it ties every later record to your pet.
2. Rabies vaccination certificate — recorded after the microchip, with dates, the microchip number and vet details all exact.
3. Veterinary health certificate — the standard UAE export document from the origin's competent authority.
4. UAE export permit / booking — arrange the export side and flight, then arrive for the CFIA import inspection in Canada.

story.lead: On the Canada route, problems are almost never quarantine — they're a certificate detail.
story.problem: An owner has their dog fully vaccinated and books the flight to Canada.
story.mistake: The rabies certificate lists a vaccination date that doesn't line up, and the microchip number isn't on it.
story.discovery: At the CFIA inspection the mismatch is flagged, and the dog is held while it's sorted.
story.result: Hours of stress at arrival and a re-issued certificate — avoidable with one document check beforehand.
story.lesson: Canada doesn't quarantine — but it does check carefully. Get the rabies certificate exact and matched to the microchip, and arrival is simple.

faqs.q: Will my pet be quarantined in Canada?
faqs.a: No. Canada doesn't quarantine pets that meet CFIA import requirements; there's an inspection on arrival instead.

faqs.q: Do I need a rabies titre test for Canada?
faqs.a: For personal pets from the UAE the central requirement is a valid rabies vaccination certificate rather than a titre test — but confirm your exact category with CFIA, as rules differ for cats, dogs and commercial imports.

faqs.q: What's the most common Canada-route mistake?
faqs.a: An inexact rabies certificate — wrong dates, or a missing microchip number — flagged at the CFIA inspection. A document check beforehand prevents it.

faqs.q: How much does Dubai → Canada cost?
faqs.a: Typically AED 14,000–20,000 depending on your pet's size and the airline, over about 4–6 weeks.

method.structure_logic: 2026 article anatomy: headline (curiosity/result) -> answer-first opening (the liftable answer in the first lines) -> key takeaways -> table of contents -> scannable H2/H3 -> a visual (data table or flow) -> original insight or a story -> FAQ -> official sources -> one help-first CTA. Why: web readers scan ~20-28% of words (Nielsen Norman Group), so the answer is front-loaded; a story is remembered where bare facts are forgotten; one page = one job + a single CTA converts. These choices recur across every source in our research (see SOURCING-METHOD.md).
method.geo_seo_rationale: What we believe helps. GEO (being cited by AI answer engines): answer-first self-contained chunks, cited statistics, official-source citations, consistent entities, FAQ schema -- and citation is decoupled from ranking (~66% of AI-Overview citations come from outside the top-20), so strong content can be cited even before it ranks. SEO: intent-matched title+H1, topical depth, internal links into the money page, visible freshness dates, structured data (Article/FAQ/Breadcrumb/LocalBusiness). HONEST CAVEAT: these are evidence-based best practices, NOT guaranteed results -- ranking also needs off-page authority/backlinks/indexing not built here, and GEO citation is plausible but unproven until measured with a live AI-citation test.
method.how_and_why_we_audit: Each page is scored by a 5-lens auditor -- Website, SEO, GEO, Lead-gen/Trust, Quality -- which together cover the 7-category QA (Helpful, Human, Original, Trustworthy, SEO, GEO, Conversion). Why this way: (1) page-type profiles judge a page against ITS job (a reassurance page is weighted differently from a money page); (2) every check carries an evidence tier (T1 sworn -> T6 practitioner) and a verified-vs-heuristic tag; (3) not-measurable checks are excluded, never zeroed (a coverage->confidence label); (4) risk caps catch keyword-stuffing, thin content, fake schema, no-CTA. The score is an on-page QUALITY PROXY, not a measured ranking/citation outcome.
method.what_we_are_sure_of: 100% sure = a fact screenshot-verified against its official source as of a date (see sourcing.verified_100pct) + that the method was applied. NOT sure = that it ranks or gets cited (unproven until the site is live, indexed and measured).
method.how_we_verify: Every factual/regulatory claim is verified against an OFFICIAL source only -- government bodies, recognised standards bodies (IATA), or the operator's own site (e.g. the airline). Never blogs, forums, competitors, or AI. Each verified claim is captured as a full-page SCREENSHOT and logged in a regulatory register with: source, URL, date verified, version, reviewer, and a re-verify-by date (because regulations change). Anything we could not confirm from an official source is HEDGED or flagged 'confirm with [authority]', never asserted (see sourcing.stated_but_unverified). Tooling: a Playwright screenshot verifier with an official-domain allowlist + the regulatory register. Facts are kept separate from advice ('the authority requires X' vs 'we recommend X'). AI never makes the final call -- a human reviews and signs off before publish.
